The dataset's tagger is switched off (VOICECLONE__TEXT__EZAFE__ENABLED=false) so its older code adds nothing: checked on this Mac, e1d96e4's text path passes all twelve unchanged, one chunk each

rendering: one Kaggle T4 x2 session on step 3's code dataset (e1d96e4), built by kaggle/build_ezafe_voices_kernel.py: scripts/benchmark.py once per form with --sentences-file, seed 42, each speaker's reference clip and its transcript; 25 x 12 = 300 renders per form, 900 in all. Held-out similarity (ECAPA against the four held-out clips) and CER are scored in the same session, the recogniser's floor by the first run. Every render's metadata must name the weights its form was given
rule: the app's OmniVoice weights become E5 if the 95% interval of E5's held-out similarity minus E1's - the mean of each speaker's paired differences, a t interval over speakers (scripts/compare_runs.py) - does not lie wholly below zero, and E5's mean CER is not more than 2 points above E1's. Otherwise they stay E1. An interval that cannot be given keeps E1
read_beside_it_not_for_the_decision: E1 and E5 against A1 the same way: if either lies wholly below zero it is said, and whether to go back to A1 is the user's call (the listening check heard A1 say 16 words wrong to E1's 6); every pair's CER; each interval beside compare_runs.py's practical reference of 0.0205

not_claimed: one seed; Neyshekar's read speech; similarity as ECAPA measures it; nobody listens in this check
